Maintenance review — 30 October 2026

Source: MAINTENANCE.md

Purpose and acceptance criteria

Retain the multiverse tic-tac-toe rules, branching history and plotting/app interfaces while making bounded search controls effective. Essential criteria are legal selected moves, reproducible fixed-work searches, meaningful ratings, controlled invalid-input errors and a checked installable package.

Evidence and changes

  • High: mxo_ai_move() ignored ..., so requested iterations/depth/budgets never reached the engine. Named overrides now reach their selected method, including time_budget = NULL; duplicate/positional overrides fail clearly.

  • High: the MCTS clock was checked only between whole rollouts. Checks now run through tree traversal and rollout operations. Hard difficulty defaults to a cooperative two-second budget. This is not a preemptive timeout: one expensive operation can overrun it. Fixed-iteration behavior remains available explicitly.

  • Medium: MCTS move ratings performed an expensive heuristic search at each rollout ply. The default now uses random rollouts; heuristic rollouts remain selectable. No claim of improved playing strength is made.

  • Medium: search ratings calculated negamax scores but ranked unrelated heuristic probabilities. Search ranks now use negamax scores; unsupported probability labels are NA. Heuristic/MCTS labels retain their existing meanings.

  • Medium: search depths could be truncated to integers; validate before conversion.

  • Low: repeated isotonic knots caused interpolation warnings, and constant-score fits lacked a defined interpolation path. Store distinct fitted knots and return the constant fit where applicable, preserving missing predictions.

  • High: the Shiny app displayed human-play modes but had no human-move handler. Added legal-move selection with stable move keys, explicit play, a human-X/AI-O reply, and step-by-step AI play. Stale selections are refused. The requested initial difficulty now reaches the UI; board rendering no longer depends on an unavailable infix helper, and startup checks its plotly dependency.

Validation

The baseline source suite exceeded its 600-second limit. The first repaired full suite passed in 239.35 seconds, with one isotonic warning subsequently repaired. The calibration regression suite passed. A complete built-package check with vignettes/examples/tests passed before the final rating-rank change. The final search regression suite passed after correcting its history-list fixture. An actual hard move returned a legal move in 2.137 seconds; two fixed-work seeded runs matched exactly. The final R CMD check --no-manual --no-tests returned Status OK, including rebuilt vignettes and examples. A fresh installation outside the checkout passed bounded AI selection, applying its legal move, undo and search-score ranking. The final check runs the package examples; the full source/packaged tests and final targeted search/calibration tests were run separately. One intermediate regression fixture accessed a history list as a data frame; that fixture was corrected and the final focused suite passed.

First use

Install the Imports from DESCRIPTION and run R CMD INSTALL .. In a new R:

library(multixoR)
g <- mxo_new_game(n = 3L, k = 3L)
m <- mxo_ai_move(g, "hard", seed = 1L)
g <- mxo_move(g, m$kind, m$L_src, m$t_src, m$idx)
ggplot2::autoplot(g)
# Optional app dependencies: shiny, bslib, DT, plotly
mxo_run_app()

For repeatable experiments, set time_budget = NULL and explicit bounded iterations/depth. Timed searches can perform different work on different CPUs.

Roadmap and boundaries

This milestone repairs control and interpretation failures without changing the rules or replacing the engine. Next: profile representative branching positions and validate calibration on held-out configurations before stronger performance or probability claims. Compiled search and new game variants remain deferred. Remote CI, Windows/Linux and CRAN are not verified for this candidate. After review, push through the existing platform matrix and inspect its exact results; no submission or deployment has occurred.

Final app verification: seven server assertions cover human play, stale move refusal, undo, reset, automatic replies and AI stepping. An installed Chromium journey confirmed initial hard difficulty, human+AI turns, undo/reset, an AI step, Board and Analysis tabs without page errors. The final app source archive passed R CMD check --no-manual --no-tests with Status OK, including examples and rebuilt vignettes (75.34-second build, 86.4-second check). Source tests and the final app regressions ran separately.
